relationship: Head-to-tail vector commands determine a route, while their resultant displacement depends on components and can remain fixed when route order changes.

learnerLoop.action: Translate, scale or reverse vector commands, build a route and run the robot.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The command route, robot path and resultant components update.
learnerLoop.evidence: The floor trace, target outcome, component display and magnitude working compare path with displacement.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Change a command or its order, then decide whether the resultant and route constraint are satisfied.

invariants: A vector's translation does not change its components.
The resultant components equal the sum of command components, even when order changes.
safeAdaptations: Vary reusable vector commands, targets and route obstacles.
Adjust working support while retaining both physical-route and component evidence.
nonGoals: Treating equal resultants as identical travelled paths.

task.description: Current vector-route stage, concept and progress.
task.visibility: Shown for the current generated route.

model.description: Grid, reusable vector sources, command route, resultant and robot trace show path and displacement.
model.visibility: Present throughout; source/route layers vary by stage and order.

working.description: Ordered command slots plus component and magnitude calculation entries.
working.visibility: Command strip is present throughout; magnitude work appears at All.

evidence.description: Live vector sums, route/displacement distances, collision/miss status and order relationship show the distinction between path and resultant.
evidence.visibility: Updates after command reorder, source translation, prediction movement and route runs.

completion.description: Successful route, insight and next route/support upgrade.
completion.visibility: Shown only after a valid run, correct prediction and required working checks.

settings.description: Working support, route run/undo, command reorder and reset controls.
settings.visibility: Controls are shown for the current route; run and reorder actions operate on the generated command strip.

inputs.description: Reusable vector/source controls, prediction marker, command order and resultant entries.
inputs.visibility: Source and command controls are generated for each route; answer inputs are always rendered but are checked only at their selected level.

source-vectors.description: Reusable vector components and, on scalar stages, the scalar multiplier.
source-vectors.output: Source labels, route segments and component chains.

route-order.description: Filled command sequence and head-to-tail endpoint, including subtraction or fractional scalar commands where supplied.
route-order.source: Command chips dropped into #commandStrip and earlier/later controls.

prediction.description: Predicted finishing point for the route.

resultant-components.description: Resultant rx and ry obtained by summing the ordered command components.
resultant-components.source: Auto calculation plus #rxInput/#ryInput when Working Some/All.

magnitude.description: Displacement magnitude from resultant components, distinct from travelled route distance.
magnitude.source: Auto result and #magInput at Working All.

modes.none: Source level 0 shows component and magnitude calculations while the learner builds and runs the route.
modes.some: Source level 1 requires resultant component entries rx and ry.
modes.all: Source level 2 additionally requires the magnitude entry.
modes.route-types: The five source stages cover order/addition, subtraction, scalar multiplication, same-resultant paths and fractional scalars with magnitude; stage flags also require translation, safe order or collision constraints as supplied.

dependencies: Every command slot must be filled and the prediction marker moved before Run; route data recomputes from the current order and source vectors.
A run can fail for collision, missed target or prediction mismatch; after a successful route, pending working answers still block completion.
At Some, rx/ry must be checked; at All, magnitude is checked after component work. Working checks become pending again after relevant changes.
The source next card appears only when the last run is valid, prediction is correct, any stage translation requirement is met and no working check is pending.
implementation.completion: The source phaseComplete check requires lastRunValid, a successful run, correct prediction, any route-specific translatedUsed flag and no pending working checks; #nextCard then exposes the next route and possible level upgrade.
limitations: Collision uses the source's segment/rack geometry and margin; prediction is a snapped grid marker rather than a typed coordinate.
Source vectors, command chips and stage-specific constraints are generated from the current route, so per-command IDs are not fixed.
